subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram onboarding retain pairing until explicit approval, or add a token-verified owner-enrollment flow that can safely write an allowlist as part of setup?
rationale: The correct first-owner authority boundary determines whether a new default is safe, how the first-run UX works, and whether existing pairing behavior remains the compatibility baseline; source inspection cannot choose that product/security policy.

options.title: Keep pairing as first-run default
options.body: Retain the current default and improve the documented/manual allowlist path for operators who want preauthorization.

options.title: Add verified owner enrollment
options.body: Require an operator-confirmed token exchange before setup persists the matching numeric Telegram sender ID as the allowlist owner.

options.title: Adopt post-bootstrap transition
options.body: Keep first-owner pairing, then evaluate the narrower cross-channel transition proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/81876.

recommendation.title: Add verified owner enrollment
recommendation.body: Require an operator-confirmed token exchange before setup persists the matching numeric Telegram sender ID as the allowlist owner.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram access-policy and setup-adjacent history plus prior direct issue follow-up make this the strongest available routing candidate.
